title: How to put in eye drops and ointment
what: How to put in drops and apply ointment inside the lower eyelid correctly so the medicine goes in the eye and not onto the cheek.
why: When your doctor prescribed eye drops or ointment, for inflammation, after surgery, or for high eye pressure.
duration: the procedure itself takes 1 to 2 minutes
tell_doctor: If several different drops were prescribed
If the drops sting for more than a couple of minutes, or the eye turns red or swells

prepare.title: Hands
prepare.text: Wash your hands before each time you put in drops.

prepare.title: Bottle
prepare.text: Check the name and expiry date. An opened bottle is usually good for a limited time, so read the leaflet.

prepare.title: Lenses
prepare.text: Usually lenses are taken out before drops. Ask your doctor when you can put them back in.

prepare.title: Several drops
prepare.text: Wait usually 5 minutes between different drops. Ointment goes last.

steps: Tilt your head back or lie down
Pull the lower eyelid down with a finger to make a small pocket
Look up and put one drop in the pocket without touching the eye with the bottle
Close your eye and lightly press the inner corner with a finger for 1 to 2 minutes
Ointment: squeeze a thin line into the pocket of the lower eyelid and close your eye
Blot any extra with a clean tissue
feel: After ointment, vision is blurry for a few minutes, which is normal
after: Ointment is easier to apply at bedtime
Do not share your drops with others
Use them for the whole course your doctor said
red_flags: Sudden eye pain, severe redness, or worse vision: see a doctor urgently
Swollen eyelids and face, or trouble breathing after drops: call emergency services

faq.q: How many drops should I use?
faq.a: Usually one. More will not fit in the eye, and the rest runs out.

faq.q: What if I'm not sure the drop went in?
faq.a: Put in one more. If you are sure it went in, do not repeat it.

reminders.text: Time for your eye drops. Hands, one drop, press the corner of the eye.
